result.stdout:
usage:
  mirror coverage
      How many natives are at each trust level, and which are Missing
  mirror check <map>
      Lists the natives a map's script calls with their trust levels
  mirror run <map> [--seconds <n>] [--seed <n>] [--hash <n>] [--record <file>] [--input <file>]
      Runs a Lua or JASS map for n simulated seconds (60) with a seed (0), then prints its log; with --hash, the state hash every n seconds; with --input, the inputs of a recording (or a list of them) at their steps; with --record, saves the run as a recording
  mirror replay <recording or .w3g> [--map <map>] [--hash <n>]
      Runs a recording again, exactly, and prints the state hash at its end (or every n seconds); a game replay (.w3g) needs its --map
  mirror desync <map> [--seconds <n>] [--seed <n>]
      Runs the map for each person's slot as that player's own game and reports where the runs first differ
  mirror snapshot <map or recording> [--at <n>] [--back <n>] [--seed <n>] [--out <file>]
      Saves the world after n simulated seconds with what it takes to run to it again; with --back, runs to --at, steps back n seconds and saves the world there
  mirror view <map or recording> [--seconds <n>] [--every <n>] [--out <file>]
      Runs it and saves a page that opens in a browser: the map from above, the units, a timeline to scrub and the log
  mirror compare <snapshot> [--map <map>]
      Runs the snapshot's run again to its step and lists what differs
  mirror test <file or folder> [--junit <file>]
      Runs the Lua tests (*.test.lua) with the Lua test API, prints each result and writes JUnit XML to the file
  mirror bench <map> [--seconds <n>] [--seed <n>]
      Times a run: how many times faster than real time it goes
  mirror fuzz <map> [--seconds <n>] [--seed <n>] [--orders <n>]
      Gives every player's units random legal orders each second and reports script errors

A map is a map file (.w3x or .w3m), a folder map (a folder of that name holding the map's files), or one named War3.w3mod:Maps/..., which is read from the ins

result.stdout:
usage:
  mirror check <map>
      Lists the natives a map's script calls with their trust levels

A map is a map file (.w3x or .w3m), a folder map (a folder of that name holding the map's files), or one named War3.w3mod:Maps/..., which is read from the installed game. Any command that takes a map also takes --users <slots> and --computers <slots> (comma separated), or --melee true to seat the first user slot with a person and the others with computers, and --graphics reforged or classic, the graphics mode the player has chosen in the game's options, whose data the run reads (Reforged unless given; a recording keeps its own).
